authority: Explicit user instruction in the 2026-11-04 Nagi OS porting-readiness task.
objective: Help third-party developers assess Rust, C, and C++ application source and manifest boundaries, follow migration guidance, and reuse portable existing application code in a separate host-buildable sample.
scope: Add a static, bounded, read-only `nagi port readiness PROJECT [--format json]` command to tools/nagi-cli.
Create samples/porting/portable-files as a separate Cargo workspace with a license-noticed portable Nagi Files core excerpt and a third-party manifest fixture.
Add English and Japanese migration guidance describing evidence, adapters, permissions, SDK boundaries, and limitations.
Use the existing package validator and keep focused tests inside the authorized CLI/sample paths.
forbidden_scope: Building, executing, installing, or launching the inspected project or any Nagi guest application.
Changing Nagi 0.1 milestones, M30 status, 0.2 runtime gates, kernel, loader, target output, SDK implementation, package-validator implementation, or first-party Nagi Files implementation.
Editing samples/hello-nagi, any SDK/package validator path, or docs/porting/multiarch owned by another active task.
Claiming arbitrary Linux binaries, general POSIX, Qt, GTK, Electron, SDL, or other framework compatibility without separate evidence.
acceptance: The report uses static text and manifest inspection only, emits bounded evidence with explicit limitations, and never certifies compatibility.
Focused host tests cover portable Rust, Rust filesystem/process use, C process/thread use, C++ GUI-framework evidence, unknown dependencies, malformed roots, and stable JSON output.
The independent Files sample builds on the host, validates with the existing package validator, and demonstrates reuse of license-compatible portable source without changing its first-party owner.
The bilingual guide explains migration assessment, the public SDK/capability boundary, required adapters, and what remains unverified.
M30 remains PARTIAL and target install/launch/runtime outcomes remain NOT_RUN.
